bull.b: The 210,600-square-foot Pendergrass facility gives NeoVolta a domestic production base and a pathway to scale beyond its historical residential model. Completing validation and repeatable workflows could improve delivery capability, support domestic-content requirements, and enable broader customer adoption.

A five-year supply agreement with SK On provides greater visibility into a critical battery input and aligns NeoVolta with U.S.-manufactured LFP cells. This supports planned capacity expansion, strengthens supply planning, and may improve the company's ability to serve larger storage deployments.

Expansion across residential, commercial and industrial, and utility-scale storage diversifies NeoVolta's potential customer base beyond traditional installers. A broader platform can support larger deployments and reduce reliance on any single market as the company develops products and channels.

bear.b: Zero reported FY2026 revenue alongside recurring large operating and net losses shows that commercialization has not yet produced a stable earnings base. Until revenue recovers and the cost structure becomes more efficient, the company remains exposed to execution risk and continued shareholder capital consumption.

Deeply negative operating and free cash flow increases NeoVolta's dependence on external financing while production and sales are being built. Accelerating burn can constrain investment flexibility and make execution more sensitive to the timing of customer orders, deliveries, and funding availability.

A substantial portion of stated demand remains prospective rather than contracted, and the company still must complete technical, quality, and customer qualification steps. Delays in converting pipeline opportunities into binding orders could postpone revenue, weaken factory utilization, and extend the investment phase.
